This hits GitHub's concurrent job limits (shared with CI and publish across all tenants), costs 40 runner-minutes of mostly install overhead, and starves publish jobs. Processing latency is runner start-up time (tens of seconds) rather than image time. Wrangler is downloaded fresh on every publish.
unverified.fix: Batch: one media job drains all unprocessed rows for a workspace (or a small queue of ids per dispatch). Cache npm with setup-node 'cache: npm' or vendor wrangler into factory/runner/package.json with npm ci. Long term, process images in an edge or Cloudflare worker (Images or WASM) and keep GitHub only for the site build.

unverified.title: Lead export holds 5,000 full lead rows in edge-function memory and writes one event row per lead in a PL/pgSQL loop
unverified.evidence: lead-export/index.ts:49-50 selects up to MAX_ROWS+1=5001 rows including the 'answers' jsonb, builds the whole CSV as one string (line 62) and returns it. Line 59 then sends all ids to service.leads_exported, which at 20261031000012_screens.sql:146-151 loops per lead: a select into l, a can_act_on_lead check, an insert into lead_events.
unverified.problem: One export means thousands of row-by-row statements in a single transaction and a CSV buffered in memory. With wide industry answers this is exposed to the edge memory and CPU limits, and the 5,000 cap silently truncates a large tenant's own data (header only). Concurrent exports from several users multiply the load, and the unbounded lead_events growth feeds the lead timeline.
unverified.fix: Make leads_exported a single set-based insert...select (join leads to unnest(ids), filtered by the policy predicate). Stream the CSV (ReadableStream with keyset pagination on created_at,id). Run exports above N rows as an async job that writes to Storage and returns a signed link.

unverified.title: Publish dispatch and the user-facing 202 are tied to a synchronous call to GitHub with an 8 s timeout; there is no outbox
unverified.evidence: publish/index.ts:32-34 commits the job (service.start_publish), then awaits dispatch() inline (dispatch.ts:14-19, AbortSignal.timeout(8000)) before answering. A failure is only reported as dispatched:false (dispatch.ts:23-26); the job is not retried by anything that runs (see the reaper finding).
unverified.problem: The request thread is held up to 8 s on a third-party API on every publish and every photo finish. A GitHub outage becomes a dashboard latency spike plus silently stranded jobs. Dispatch is not atomic with the job insert, so there is no at-least-once guarantee.
unverified.fix: Write the job and an outbox row in one transaction. A scheduled dispatcher (cron) sends pending outbox rows with retry and backoff and marks them sent. The request returns 202 immediately.

refuted.title: Deploy and key-minting tooling is hard-wired to one staging project, with no environment model for production
refuted.reason: The staging-only naming in tools/deploy-functions.mjs:5,24 is by design: docs/product/2-architecture.md:94-100 rules that the working repo never holds a production key and that production changes only through the owner-run promote workflow in a separate private repo, and .github/production/promote.yml:164-172 already deploys functions to production with PROD_SUPABASE_REF through that same tool (plus read-only smoke checks), so the production path exists and the "no environment model" claim is wrong (at most a low naming/env-var-aliasing nit).

notCovered: Tenant-owned content rendered into the static sites (factory/ templates and renderer, plus the public form script): is every client-supplied string (headings, rich text, image URLs, JSON-LD, form labels) escaped or sanitised per output context? A grep for escapeHtml, sanitize and innerHTML in factory/ returned zero hits, so the escaping strategy is unconfirmed. Also whether a compromised or malicious workspace member can inject script into a live production client site.

Custom domains and TLS lifecycle: docs/product/2-architecture.md:80 says domains are handled by pointing nameservers at an Omnikom Cloudflare zone, but a repo grep for custom_domain, domain verification and custom-hostnames found nothing. Where is domain add, verify, DNS and certificate renewal automated, how is domain takeover or dangling-record risk handled on offboarding, and how is one tenant stopped from claiming another's hostname?

Tenant lifecycle, offboarding and data portability: supabase/migrations and functions have no visible workspace-delete, export-everything or off-boarding path. Does the architecture's 'leaving is pointing the nameservers back' promise hold for leads, media and content, and who deletes the Pages project, the storage objects and the DNS zone? Also whether the shipped CSV export is a full export. This is distinct from the auth.users FK finding because it is about the whole workspace.

Lead-data compliance and email deliverability: capture-lead stores consent text (supabase/functions/capture-lead/index.ts:69), but is there any suppression or unsubscribe record, consent withdrawal, consent version history, DMARC/SPF/DKIM setup for the alert sender, bounce or complaint handling for Resend, or a data-subject access path (GDPR, CCPA, TCPA, CAN-SPAM)? Grep for unsubscribe, bounce and dmarc in supabase/functions returned only the consent text.

Billing, plans and entitlements: no Stripe, plan-limit or entitlement code exists in supabase/ or apps/dashboard/src (grep returned nothing). Where are per-tenant quotas (sites, leads, media bytes, publishes per day) defined and enforced, and what stops one tenant exhausting shared Cloudflare, Resend and GitHub Actions capacity? The existing quota-circuit-breaker finding covers vendor spend, not per-tenant fairness or the paid product model.

Staff and admin authority model and audit trail: supabase/functions/_shared/dashboard.ts and the staff path. Is there an append-only audit log of privileged staff actions (cross-workspace reads, support access, role grants), staff MFA enforcement, session lifetime and revocation, and a documented break-glass procedure? A grep of migrations for audit_log, staff_action and impersonation matched only platform.sql, crm.sql and addons.sql, so confirm whether those are real audit tables.

Cross-origin trust for the public capture endpoint: _shared/dashboard.ts:36 reflects an Origin into access-control-allow-origin, and capture-lead is called from every client's domain. Is there a per-site allowed-origin list checked against the site's registered domains, or can any page post leads to any workspace's site key? Also check how the site key is minted, rotated and revoked.

Schema change and release governance: migrations are forward-only (latest supabase/migrations/20261105000018_lead_list_site.sql) and apply-staging.mjs applies them to staging. Is there a CI job that replays all migrations on a clean database, checks drift between staging and production, runs a migration linter for locks and backward compatibility, and defines a rollback or expand-contract policy? Also no .github/dependabot.yml or equivalent automated dependency-update and vulnerability-audit job exists, though actions are SHA-pinned.
